claims.statement: For the SSH chain with intra-cell hopping v and inter-cell hopping w (v, w rational, nonzero, |v| != |w|): the open chain with 2N+1 sites has nullity(H) = 1 exactly, with kernel vector psi_A(n) = (-v/w)^n on A sites and 0 on B sites; the open chain with 2N sites has rank(H) = 2N exactly (no zero mode), because det(D) = v^N for its lower-bidiagonal sublattice block D. Verified on 6 rational (v,w) instances x 3 chain sizes (N = 2, 3, 5) = 18 parameter points, in exact fractions.Fraction arithmetic (no floating point).

Positive control demonstrated to fire: PC1 (v=0 decoupled-site chain triggers the zero-mode detector), guarding against a rank/nullity check that never reports a zero mode.

claims.statement: For the same instances: the zero mode of the odd chain is concentrated at the left end (|psi_A(0)| > |psi_A(N)|) if and only if |w| > |v|.

claims.statement: For h(z) = v + wz on the counterclockwise unit circle |z| = 1 with |v/w| < 1 (pole inside), (1/2*pi*i) * oint h'(z)/h(z) dz = 1, by Mathlib's circleIntegral.integral_sub_inv_of_mem_ball (h'/h = (z + v/w)^-1, a simple pole at -v/w inside the ball). The case |v/w| > 1 (pole outside) is not covered by that lemma and needs Cauchy's theorem for a pole outside the contour; the exact Mathlib name for that step has not yet been identified.

claims.statement: CORRECTED 2026-09-27 (v2). On an SSH ring of L cells (|w|>|v|, subsystem of ell whole cells severing two w-bonds), the two entanglement levels closest to 1/2 form an exact chiral pair z1+z2=1 and sit at |z-1/2| ~ (v/w)^min(ell, L-ell): ordinary exponential finite-size smearing, with decay length fitted within 15% of xi = 1/ln(w/v) at r = 0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 (L=200). They are pinned to 1/2 EXACTLY only at ell = L/2, where a reflection through the two cuts combined with chiral symmetry cancels the hybridisation. When |v|>|w| no level is near 1/2. Version 1 of this claim stated there was NO finite-size smearing and explained it as a quantised invariant that cannot smear; that was an artefact of measuring only ell = L/2 (at two ring sizes) and is retracted. Positive and negative controls stand.

claims.statement: For the 4-body Majorana SYK model (N Majoranas, N % 4 == 0, exact diagonalization), the exact-degeneracy rate of the parity-sector ground state is a clean all-or-nothing function of N mod 8 at every tested N <= 24: 0/40 realizations degenerate at N in {8, 16, 24} (N mod 8 = 0), 40/40 at N in {12, 20} (N mod 8 = 4). claims.statement: On layer-truncated hyperbolic {7,3} tilings vs Euclidean square/triangular disks (same node counts), the condition number of the boundary-to-bulk inverse-conductance Jacobian grows only polynomially with N for the hyperbolic case and super-polynomially (locally exp(c*depth) with depth ~ sqrt(N)) for the Euclidean case. Preregistered confirmatory point (L=4, N=847, not previously computed): predicted log10(cond) = 4.2 +/- 0.5, measured 3.89 (within band); max depth predicted 7, measured 7 (exact). At matched N~800-850, log10(cond) = 3.89 (hyperbolic) vs 11.77 (square) vs 11.71 (triangular): a 7.9-decade gap, wider than the 6.4-decade gap measured at N~315-320 in the prior exploratory pass. Unplanned but consistent finding: the hyperbolic graph stays full rank at every tested size (up to 1078/1078 at N=847), while the Euclidean graphs develop growing rank deficiency (up to 1143/3071 unidentifiable edges at N=1069).
claims.notes: SUPERSEDED IN PART by H0-X-0002 (kappa reporting bug) and H0-B-0001 (rank-deficiency claim retracted). Kept as the record of the original, since-corrected run; not to be cited alone. experiments/track_h_hyperbolic_network/{HYPOTHESIS.md,PREREGISTRATION.md,RESULTS.md,hyperbolic_network.py} (45/45 self-test checks pass, incl. exact-vs-finite-difference Jacobian cross-check to 1.15e-11). Original HYPOTHESIS.md claimed exponential (not polynomial) edge-sensitivity decay on FLAT lattices by direct analogy to continuum Calderon-problem instability; an external reviewer showed this derivation was dimensionally inconsistent (Poisson-kernel decay is polynomial), so an unlocked exploratory pass was run before any prediction was locked, and the mechanism was revised in HYPOTHESIS.md (dated, original argument left visible) to: exponential decay in DEPTH is common to both geometries, but depth itself scales as log N (hyperbolic) vs sqrt N (flat). Real code bugs found and fixed before this result, all now caught mechanically in self_test(): boundary classification used vertex degree (misses rim-junction vertices) rather than face incidence; a triangular-lattice face had a non-adjacent vertex offset, breaking the Euler characteristic check (caught: V-E+F=-5 instead of 1); the finite-difference Jacobian's eps=1e-6 imposed a ~1e-10-relative floor on resolvable singular values, replaced by the exact harmonic-extension formula dLambda/dg_e=(P_a-P_b)^T(P_a-P_b). Novelty search bounded (2 queries): found 1107.0343 (Borcea, Druskin, Guevara Vasquez & Mamonov -- NOT 'Deban, Borcea et al.' as first mis-cited here, corrected in H0-X-0002) and 1104.4858 (Ervedoza & de Gournay); reported as 'not found in this search', not 'novel'. [EVIDENCE BLOB NOT RECOVERED: no tracked file hashes to this digest; the gate with --evidence-dir reports it. Statement unchanged.]

claims.statement: CORRECTS H0-X-0001. The kappa this script reported was capped by its own rank-tolerance formula (kappa = s_max/s[rank-1], and s[rank-1] > tol = s_max*max(J.shape)*eps by construction, so kappa < 1/(max(J.shape)*eps) ALWAYS) -- not by float64's true precision floor, which H0-X-0001 wrongly attributed the large-N flat-lattice 'plateau' to. Verified: the reported 'saturated' log10(kappa) for the 3 largest flat cases matched log10(1/(max(J.shape)*eps)) to 4 significant figures. Corrected: kappa is now the RAW untruncated ratio s_max/s_min, and cases where s_min rounds to float64 noise are reported as NUMERICALLY SINGULAR, not as a finite number. Net effect: the corrected result is STRONGER. Points unaffected by the bug (all {7,3} L=1..4; flat lattices at N<=317) are unchanged -- the 6.4-decade gap at N~315-320 (log10 kappa 3.27 vs 9.72) stands. At N~800-850, the hyperbolic lattice remains measurable (3.89) while the flat lattice's Jacobian is correctly reported as beyond float64's ability to assign ANY condition number -- a stronger separation than a finite decade count. Also corrects a citation error: 1107.0343's authors are Borcea, Druskin, Guevara Vasquez & Mamonov, not 'Deban, Borcea et al.' as first (wrongly) attributed from a search snippet without checking papers/meta/.

Does NOT correct the rank-deficiency claim in H0-X-0001 (a separate bug on a separate quantity) -- see H0-B-0001. claims.statement: RETRACTS the rank-deficiency claim in H0-X-0001 (e.g. triangular N=1069: 1143/3071 'unidentifiable' edges), for the sizes tested here. Exact rank certified by modular arithmetic (GF(p), two independent primes, agreement required) over the SAME harmonic-extension Jacobian construction: {7,3} L=1 (E=42) and L=2 (E=140) are FULL RANK, certified. Flat lattices: square N=113 (E=200) and triangular N=187 (E=502) are FULL RANK, certified (agreeing with float64 at these unsaturated sizes). DECISIVE: triangular N=475 (E=1331), a size comparable to the N=421 instance float64 reported as deficient (102/1176), is EXACTLY FULL RANK, certified across both primes. The float64 'structural deficiency' was a numerical-precision artefact, not a genuine algebraic property. Consequence: H1's real content is NOT a difference in structural identifiability between hyperbolic and flat boundary-to-bulk inverse problems (both are exactly full rank at these sizes) -- it is a difference in CONDITIONING, i.e. the precision required to exploit that full rank, which grows polynomially (hyperbolic) vs super-polynomially, past float64's representable range by N~1000 (flat).

Any future prose using 'structurally unrecoverable' for the flat-lattice case must be corrected against this entry. claims.statement: The bottom of the spectrum lambda_0 of the combinatorial Laplacian of an infinite graph of bounded degree is positive iff its edge-isoperimetric (Cheeger) constant is positive [Dodziuk, Trans. AMS 284 (1984) 787-794; Mohar, Linear Algebra Appl. 103 (1988) 119-131]; the {7,3} tiling graph has an explicit positive isoperimetric constant [Haggstrom, Jonasson & Lyons, Ann. Probab. 30 (2002) 443-473].

Flat disks have lambda_min -> 0.
